questions.question:
**In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

Someone have walked away with my umbrella.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'have walked'. **

__
 
• The erroneous part **'have walked'** should be **'has walked'. **
 
• We know that 'each, every, everyone. someone, somebody, nobody, none, one, any, many a, more than one' are singular in meaning.
 
• Therefore, a singular helping verb/ singular pronoun should be used after them. 
 
 
• *Example: Each student has come. *
 
 
 
• Hence, in the given sentence, **'has'** should be used. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 ​

**Correct sentence:__** *Someone **has walked** away with my umbrella. *

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of "**has being**" which is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be "**has been**" to properly convey the present perfect tense.
 
• The phrase should read "**has been** a masterpiece", ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

**Correct Sentence:** *"The artist believes that this new collection of paintings **has been** a masterpiece that will redefine contemporary art."*

questions.question:
**Direction: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

We are yet living in the same house.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****yet living​.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The part 'yet living' is incorrect as it is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The meaning of the word** 'yet'** is used with negative verbs or in questions for talking about something that has not happened but that you expect to happen.
 
• 
 
 
• Example:* **Has it stopped raining **yet**?*
 
 
 
• *​*An infinitive verb is essentially the base form of a verb with the word** "to" **in front of it.
 
• When you use an infinitive verb, the "to" is a part of the verb.
 
• The structure 'to + V1' to show that the next word is an infinitive verb.
 
 
• Example:* **I want to go there.*
 
 
 
• *​*Therefore, the use of **'yet living****'** in the sentence should be replaced with 'yet to live' to make it grammatically correct.​
 
• The correct sentence__:* **We are **yet to live **in the same house.​*

*​ * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• The past indefinite tense, also known as simple past tense, is used to indicate a finished or completed action/task that occurred/happened at a specific point in time in the past. 

 
 
• Structure: Subject + verb in the past form + . . . . . + adverb of time + . . . . .
 
• Example: *I ate a mango a few minutes ago.*
 
 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__***

__
 
• भाग 'yet living' गलत है क्योंकि यह व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है।
 
• शब्द 'yet' का प्रयोग नकारात्मक क्रियाओं के साथ या प्रश्नों में किसी ऐसी बात के बारे में बात करने के लिए किया जाता है जो हुआ नहीं है लेकिन आप होने की उम्मीद करते हैं।
 
• 
 
 
• Example:* **Has it stopped raining yet?*
 
 
 
• एक इनफिनिटिव क्रिया अनिवार्य रूप से एक क्रिया का मूल रूप है जिसके सामने **"to"** शब्द होता है।
 
• जब आप एक अपरिमेय क्रिया का उपयोग करते हैं, तो "to" क्रिया का एक भाग होता है।
 
• संरचना 'to + V1' यह दिखाने के लिए कि अगला शब्द एक अपरिमेय क्रिया है।
 
 
• Example:* **I want to go there.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, व्याकरण की दृष्टि से इसे सही बनाने के लिए वाक्य में 'yet living' के उपयोग को 'yet to live' से बदल दिया जाना चाहिए।

questions.question:
**Direction: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error'.**

I am thirty-two years old, and my sister are fifteen.
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"my sister are fifteen."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error in the sentence is a subject-verb agreement issue.
 
• The reason to use **"is" **instead of **"are"** is to ensure subject-verb agreement.
 
• In the sentence, **"my sister"** is a singular subject, and therefore, it requires a singular verb.
 
• **"Is"** is the correct form for the third-person singular present tense of the verb **"to be."**
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *I am thirty-two years old, and **my sister is fifteen**__. *

The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of "**have**" instead of "**has**" to match the singular subject "**Mr. Surya**."
 
• The correct verb form for the singular subject should be "**has**".
 
• The correct phrase should be "**has no interior**," ensuring grammatical correctness and subject-verb agreement.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Mr. Surya **has no interior** motive in offering you support."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The secretary __talks __over the phone right now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'is talking'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the third-person singular present form of the verb 'talks' is incorrect.
 
• The phrase "**right now**" **indicates** that the given sentence is in the present continuous tense. 
 
• We use the present continuous tense when an action or condition is happening now, frequently, and may continue into the future.
 
• The Present Continuous Formula: to be (am, is, are) + verb (the present participle).
 
• The present continuous form of the verb "is talking" should be used in place of "talks".

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence__: *The secretary **is talking** over the phone right now*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

I goes to / attend dance classes at / the National Dance Academy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the verb 'goes' is incorrect.
 
• The subject **'I'** is **first person singular** and should be used with the verb **'go'** to form **'I go'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'go' instead of 'goes'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *I go to attend dance classes at the National Dance Academy*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The subject **'I'** always takes the base form of the verb without the 's' ending.
 
• In English, the third person singular pronouns (he, she, it) are the ones that take a verb with an 's' ending in the present simple tense.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is:** she will become topper**.

• **"would"** should be in the place of **"will"** as the sentence is given in** indirect speech.**
 
• The article **"the"** is used to specify a **particular noun**.
 
 
• For example: He is the man for this job.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, the article **'the' **is used for indicating that Jaya will be the top student in her class.
 
• The phrase "she will become topper" is missing the necessary article **"the" **before "topper."
 
• The correct form should be **"she would become the topper."**

The corrected sentence should be: *Jaya said that she **would** become **the **topper in her class*.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I will celebrating New Year at my old residence as usual.

options.text: at my old residence as usual.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**will celebrating**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'will celebrating' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the correct form should use **future tense** with **'will be celebrating'**.
 
• The auxiliary verb '**will**' should be followed by '**be**' and the present participle (verb+ing) form.
 
• **Correct form**: 'I **will be celebrating** New Year at my old residence as usual.'

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *I **will be celebrating** New Year at my old residence as usual*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 'I'** - This part of the sentence is correct as it is the subject of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: 'New Year'** - This part is correct as it specifies the occasion being celebrated.
 
• **Option 4: 'at my old residence as usual.'** - This part is correct as it specifies the location and the regularity of the event.

questions.question:
**Directions: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

The manager said that Rahul does not wants to go to Mumbai for the new project.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. does not wants .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"does not wants"** is grammatically incorrect because the auxiliary verb **"does"** requires the base form of the main verb.
 
• The correct form should be **"does not want"**, not **"does not wants"**.
 
• This is a rule in English grammar where auxiliary verbs like **"do/does"** are followed by the base form of the verb (without adding -s).

Correct sentence: *The manager said that Rahul does not want to go to Mumbai for the new project.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule for Auxiliary Verbs:**

 
 
• When using auxiliary verbs like **"do/does"** in negative sentences, always use the base form of the main verb.
 
• Example: **She does not like chocolate.** (Correct) vs. **She does not likes chocolate.** (Incorrect).
 
 
 
• **Common Auxiliary Verbs:**
 
 
• **Do/Does:** Used for present tense.
 
• **Did:** Used for past tense.
 
• Always followed by the base verb.

It is not possible to discuss anything with her because of her angry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., because of her angry.**

The sentence uses the __incorrect adjective form__ **'angry**', which must be used along with some other noun, such as angry man etc.

Given the context of the sentence, which directly refers to it, __the word should be present in its noun form__, viz., **anger**.

Thus, the rectified sentence is: It is not possible to discuss anything with her **because of her anger.**
